messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The DOI/URL exactly matches the source record: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12302-023-00716-5.
The source is described as pilot-scale column investigations in a peer-reviewed article, consistent with classification as pilot_or_field_deployment.
Locator WEB03-E02 states that GAC column tests were used to determine the operation time of a full-scale GAC adsorber, clearly indicating a pilot-scale GAC column used for scale-up purposes.

WEB03-E02 explicitly states that the pilot-scale GAC adsorber received contaminated groundwater and PFAS concentrations were measured, which supports the matrix description as contaminated groundwater containing PFAS.

WEB03-E01 and WEB03-E02 describe granular activated carbon (GAC) column tests for PFAS, supporting the treatment description as GAC adsorption in a pilot-scale adsorber treating PFAS-contaminated groundwater.
WEB03-E01, E03, and E04 describe breakthrough curves and specific throughput (bed volumes) until C/C0 reaches certain values, which are standard measures of removal performance in adsorption columns.

WEB03-E01, E03, and E04 describe breakthrough curves, 10% breakthrough, and C/C0≈1, matching the interpretation of PFAS removal characterized by bed volumes at first breakthrough, 10% C/C0, and C/C0≈1.

WEB03-E02 states that GAC column tests were used to determine operation time of a full-scale adsorber, that the adsorber received contaminated groundwater, and PFAS concentrations were measured at different bed depths. This supports the configuration description of a pilot-scale GAC column adsorber with measurements at different bed depths operated to breakthrough.
The configuration field is descriptive and correctly leaves unit as null; the source does not provide a numeric unit for configuration.

WEB03-E04 and E05 describe a 10% breakthrough and specify that under the given boundary conditions a 10% breakthrough was used as a maximum, supporting the description of the breakthrough criterion as 10% of the influent concentration.
The breakthrough criterion is expressed as a fraction of influent concentration, not a physical unit, so leaving unit null is appropriate and consistent with the text.
PFBA is explicitly mentioned in WEB03-E01, E03, and E04 as a PFAS with reported breakthrough behavior, supporting its inclusion in PFAS scope.
PFPeA is explicitly mentioned in WEB03-E04 with a reported 10% breakthrough bed volume, supporting its inclusion in PFAS scope.
PFHxA is explicitly mentioned in WEB03-E04 and E05 as having 10% breakthrough and being effectively removed, supporting its inclusion in PFAS scope.
PFHpA is explicitly mentioned in WEB03-E04 and E05 with 10% breakthrough information and effectiveness discussion, supporting its inclusion in PFAS scope.
PFOA is explicitly mentioned in WEB03-E01, E04, and E05 with breakthrough and effectiveness information, supporting its inclusion in PFAS scope.
WEB03-E03 states that PFBA breakthrough could be observed at 5,000 bed volumes, matching the recorded value of 5000.
WEB03-E03 gives 5,000 bed volumes (BV), supporting the unit BV for PFBA breakthrough at first observation.
WEB03-E03 reports that at 11,000 BV the effluent and initial concentration were equal (C/C0≈1), matching the recorded value 11000 for PFBA exhaustion.
WEB03-E03 specifies 11,000 BV for the point where effluent equals influent, supporting the unit BV.
WEB03-E04 reports a 10% breakthrough at 6000 BV for PFBA, matching the recorded value 6000.
WEB03-E04 expresses the 10% breakthrough in bed volumes (BV), so the unit BV is correct.
WEB03-E04 reports 10% breakthrough for PFPeA at 11,000 BV, matching the recorded value 11000.
WEB03-E04 uses bed volumes (BV) for the 10% breakthrough values, so BV is the correct unit for PFPeA.
WEB03-E04 reports 10% breakthrough for PFHxA at 16,000 BV, matching the recorded value 16000.
WEB03-E04 expresses 10% breakthrough in BV, supporting the BV unit for PFHxA.
WEB03-E04 reports 10% breakthrough for PFHpA at 20,000 BV, matching the recorded value 20000.
WEB03-E04 uses BV for 10% breakthrough, so BV is the correct unit for PFHpA.
WEB03-E04 reports 10% breakthrough for PFOA at 23,000 BV, matching the recorded value 23000.
WEB03-E04 presents the PFOA 10% breakthrough in bed volumes (BV), supporting the BV unit.

WEB03-E02 to E05 show a pilot-scale GAC column treating contaminated groundwater with PFAS-specific breakthrough and bed volumes reported at a common 10% breakthrough criterion, which reasonably supports the analyst classification of results as comparable_with_conditions across PFAS under consistent conditions.

The stated reason accurately reflects the pilot-scale GAC column in real groundwater, the use of a 10% breakthrough criterion, and reporting of specific bed volumes at breakthrough as shown in WEB03-E02 to E05.

WEB03-E05 notes that conclusions are drawn under given boundary conditions, especially initial PFAS concentrations and a 10% maximum breakthrough. The record’s statement correctly reflects dependence on influent concentration and a 10% criterion but additionally specifies the groundwater matrix and explicitly states that effectiveness and run lengths may differ, which is a reasonable but somewhat extended inference beyond the exact author wording.

WEB03-E02 describes a single pilot GAC adsorber used for determining full-scale operation time. From this design fact, inferring that a single pilot configuration may not represent all full-scale GAC systems is a justified design_inferred limitation.

WEB03-E05 states that GAC removal is effective for PFOA, PFHpA, and PFHxA but not effective or results in short operation times for PFBA and PFPeA under the given boundary conditions. The record correctly captures the relative effectiveness but adds the inferred implication about residual short-chain PFAS in treated water near end of run, which is reasonable yet goes beyond the explicit text.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, matrix (contaminated groundwater), treatment (pilot-scale GAC column), endpoint type (removal via breakthrough/bed volumes), operating conditions (pilot column with 10% breakthrough criterion), PFAS scope, and all quantitative bed-volume findings and units—are directly supported by the cited excerpts without contradictions. Minor extensions in limitation and residuals wording are interpretive but do not affect quantitative or core design information, so the record remains usable for synthesis.
